chapters.desc: The opening of the fixture: the author, the praise, and the purpose of the poem.

verses.tr: Says he who constantly hopes for the mercy of the Oft-Forgiving, forever, Sulayman Al-Jamzuri.
verses.ur: کہتا ہے وہ جو ہمیشہ بخشنے والے کی رحمت کا امیدوار ہے، یعنی سلیمان جمزوری۔

exp.en:
The author opens by naming himself, as poets of didactic verse customarily do, and by describing himself as one who hopes for mercy.

رَاجِي رَحۡمَةِ الۡغَفُورِ
exp.ur: مصنف اپنا نام ذکر کر کے آغاز کرتا ہے۔

verses.tr: All praise is due to Allah, while invoking blessings upon Muhammad, his family, and whoever follows [his path/recites].

sadrW.g: All praise is due to Allāh

verses.ur: تمام تعریفیں اللہ کے لیے ہیں، محمد پر، ان کی آل پر اور ہر اس شخص پر درود بھیجتے ہوئے جس نے «تَلَا» یعنی پیروی کی۔

verses.tr: As for what follows: This poetic arrangement is for the seeker [of knowledge], regarding the rules of Nūn Sākinah, Tanwīn, and Mudūd (prolongations).
I named it Tuhfat Al-Atfal ("A Gift for Novices/Children"), as transmitted from our teacher Al-Mihi, possessor of perfection.
I hope thereby that it will benefit the students, and [I seek through it] reward, acceptance, and divine compensation.

chapters.en: Rulings of Nūn Sākinah and Tanwīn
chapters.note: A chapter-level note, shown above the verses.

verses.tr: For the Nūn when it carries no vowel (sākinah) and for the Tanwīn, there are four rulings, so take my clear explanation:
verses.exp: The four rulings are listed in the abyāt that follow: iẓhār, idghām, iqlāb and ikhfāʾ.

verses.tr: The first is Al-Iẓhār (Clear Pronunciation) before the throat letters; there are six arranged in order, so know them:
Hamzah (ء) then Hā’ (هـ), then ‘Ayn (ع) and Ḥā’ (ح) without points, then Ghayn (غ) and Khā’ (خ).
